project.name: ApexOps — AI Assistant (BYOK)
project.description: Surface the already-hardened POST /api/ai/chat as a collapsible right-hand assistant panel, and let each user spend their own provider API key, stored encrypted at rest and never returned to the client.
project.stack: React 19 + TypeScript + Vite + Tailwind v4 + motion/react | Express + Prisma + Postgres | Node crypto AES-256-GCM | Google Generative Language API (gemini-2.5-flash)

features.description: Envelope encryption primitives exist and are correct (lib/crypto.ts)
steps: encrypt(plain) returns { ciphertext, iv, authTag }; decrypt of that triple returns the exact original string
Two encrypt() calls on identical input produce different ciphertext and different iv (fresh 12-byte IV per write)
FAILURE CASE: flipping one character of authTag makes decrypt throw, not return garbage
FAILURE CASE: AI_KEY_SECRET unset or not 32 bytes makes the module throw at call time with a named error, and there is no code path that stores plaintext instead
mask('AIzaSyABCD...WXYZ4f2c') returns first-4 + elision + last-4 and never the middle
npm test -- crypto is green, and the tamper case genuinely fails when the assertion is inverted
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15. 18 tests green; full server suite 91 green; tsc --noEmit clean. Tamper case observed FAILING when inverted to .not.toThrow(), then restored — the assertion is load-bearing, not decorative. Derivation is scryptSync over a constant salt (documented: the input is a high-entropy server secret, not a password) and is cached against the secret so rotation re-derives. Base64 chosen for all three parts and asserted, because Node's Buffer default is hex.

features.description: AI_KEY_SECRET is documented, distinct from JWT_SECRET, and absent from tracked source
steps: .env.example gains AI_KEY_SECRET with a generation command and a comment saying it must differ from JWT_SECRET
Secret scan over the tracked tree returns clean; no key material in any harness file or commit
Server refuses to start OR key endpoints answer 503 when AI_KEY_SECRET is missing — chosen behaviour documented, not accidental
FAILURE CASE: setting AI_KEY_SECRET equal to JWT_SECRET produces a startup warning
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15. .env.example documents AI_KEY_SECRET with a randomBytes(32) generation command and the rotation consequence. .env is gitignored (.gitignore:22). Secret scan over the new files is clean. Behaviour chosen and documented: production THROWS on missing / <32 chars / equal-to-JWT_SECRET (all three observed throwing under NODE_ENV=production); dev warns and uses an obvious non-random fallback, matching lib/jwtSecrets.ts. The shared-secret warning was observed in dev. Crucially the dev fallback still ENCRYPTS — there is no plaintext path.

features.description: UserAiKey model migrated; User back-relation in place
steps: Dev server on :3000 stopped before prisma generate (Windows EPERM), then generate + schema apply both succeed
user_ai_keys table exists with unique user_id, and columns ciphertext, iv, auth_tag, masked_key, verified_at, provider
Deleting a user cascades the key row away (onDelete: Cascade)
FAILURE CASE: inserting a second row for the same user_id violates the unique constraint
npm run typecheck is green at the server workspace
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15. IMPORTANT CORRECTION TO THE SPEC: this repo has NO database/prisma/migrations/ directory — it has never used `prisma migrate`, and the prior sprint (daily-note-rich-editor.md:162) applied schema changes with `prisma db push`. Running `prisma migrate dev` as the spec originally said would have made Prisma treat the populated database as drifted and offer to RESET it. Applied with `db push` instead, after previewing the exact SQL via `prisma migrate diff --script`: purely additive — one CREATE TABLE, one unique index, one cascade FK, zero DROP or ALTER of existing tables. Verified against the live database: all 10 columns present with correct types and verified_at nullable; unique index user_ai_keys_user_id_key exists; FAILURE CASE observed — a second row for the same user_id is rejected with Prisma P2002; cascade confirmed by deleting a user and counting 0 remaining key rows. Both behavioural checks ran inside transactions that were rolled back, and a residue count afterwards confirmed 0 stray rows and 0 stray users. Server stopped before generate (no EPERM) and restarted; tsc --noEmit clean, 91 server tests green, /api/health reports database connected.

features.description: PUT /api/ai/key validates against the provider before writing anything
steps: A structurally invalid key is rejected on shape alone, before any network call is made
A well-shaped but wrong key is rejected by the list-models probe with 400 INVALID_KEY
FAILURE CASE: after a rejected save, SELECT count(*) FROM user_ai_keys is unchanged — the write happens only after the probe passes
The probe uses list-models, not generateContent, so validation spends no tokens
A valid key returns { provider, maskedKey, verifiedAt } and the row now holds ciphertext, not the key
Unauthenticated PUT answers 401
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 against the running server with a real Gemini key supplied by the user. Observed: malformed key -> 400 INVALID_KEY with rows 0->0 (rejected on shape, no network call); provider='openai' -> 400 INVALID_PROVIDER; well-shaped BOGUS key -> 400 INVALID_KEY with rows 0->0, which is the failure case that matters (the probe runs before the write); real key -> 200 with maskedKey 'AIza…dIl0' and verifiedAt set; a second save upserts to 1 row, not 2; stored ciphertext does not contain the plaintext; iv is 16 base64 chars (12 bytes). DESIGN IMPROVEMENT over api/ai.ts: the probe sends the key in the 'x-goog-api-key' HEADER rather than Google's documented '?key=' query parameter. ai.ts:153-157 documents that a fetch error's message can carry the request URL and therefore the key — the header removes that leak class entirely. Probe endpoint is list-models, confirmed to return 200/50 models for a valid key and 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT for a bogus one, spending zero tokens. PROVIDER_UNREACHABLE is deliberately 503 and NOT 400: a network failure is not proof the key is bad, and saying so would cost a user a working credential.

features.description: GET and DELETE /api/ai/key are scoped to the caller and leak nothing
steps: GET returns the masked form only; the handler's Prisma select does not name ciphertext at all
GET with no stored key returns null (200), not 404 — absence is a normal state
DELETE removes the row; a second DELETE is idempotent and still 200/204
FAILURE CASE: user A's token cannot read or delete user B's key — no route accepts a userId parameter
No admin route exists anywhere that reads another user's key
Unauthenticated GET/DELETE answer 401
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15. GET/PUT/DELETE all answer 401 unauthenticated. GET with no stored key returns 200 with key=null (absence is a normal state, not a 404). The handler's Prisma select names only provider/maskedKey/verifiedAt/updatedAt — 'ciphertext' appears in zero response bodies across the whole lifecycle. DELETE is idempotent: 200, then 200 again, rows 0. CROSS-USER ISOLATION verified with two real sessions rather than argued from the code: the dev ADMIN account's GET returned key=null (its own absent key, not the user's), the admin's DELETE left the user's row intact, and GET /api/ai/key/<userId> returns 404 because no route accepts a userId at all. The absence of an admin read path is the feature.

features.description: Plaintext key material never appears in any response, log, or error across a full lifecycle
steps: Run save -> GET -> send a message -> trigger a provider error -> delete, capturing all server stdout/stderr and all HTTP response bodies
grep the captured output for the full key string: zero hits
grep for the key's middle segment (defeats naive masking): zero hits
FAILURE CASE: force a fetch failure whose err.message embeds the request URL (which carries ?key=), and confirm the handler logs it but returns none of it
Browser devtools network tab over the same lifecycle shows no plaintext key in any response body
No key material is written to localStorage, sessionStorage, or IndexedDB
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15. Full lifecycle run: save -> get -> send (real provider round trip) -> provider error on the user's own key -> rejected save -> delete, capturing all 7 response bodies plus the server's stdout/stderr to a file. Results: full key 0 hits in bodies, 0 in server log; key middle segment 0 and 0; any 'AIza' prefix 0 in the log; 'ciphertext' 0 in bodies. METHOD NOTE THAT MATTERED: the first attempt used preview_logs, whose searches returned 'no match' for the key — but also 'no match' for strings that were definitely logged, so the capture was not live and the negative result proved NOTHING. Re-run against a server started with stdout/stderr redirected to a file, and only trusted after confirming the log DID contain the handler lines ('AI provider rejected credentials: API key not valid...' and '[ai-key] provider rejected a key during validation: 400 INVALID_ARGUMENT') — i.e. the provider's message is logged, the key never is. FAILURE CASE: ai.ts was temporarily repointed at an unreachable host to force the catch block; the response was 502 PROVIDER_ERROR containing no URL and no key, while the log got only the stack trace. ai.ts restored and confirmed by an empty git diff plus a live call returning PONG. CLIENT: localStorage/sessionStorage/IndexedDB/cookies scanned in the browser — zero key material; only 'theme' and 'apexops.assistant.open' present.

features.description: resolveKey() implements BYOK -> env -> NO_KEY without weakening the existing caps
steps: With a stored key, the outbound call uses it (verify by storing a key valid for a different project and observing the attribution or the distinct error)
With no stored key and GEMINI_API_KEY set, the request still succeeds — existing behaviour preserved
With neither, the response is 503 with code NO_KEY, distinguishable from the generic unconfigured 503
FAILURE CASE: a row whose authTag has been corrupted falls through to the env key rather than erroring, and logs only the user id
CRITICAL ORDERING: an 8001-character prompt returns 400 and produces NO outbound request (confirm by network capture or provider-side counter) — resolveKey must not run before validateChatBody
The decrypted key is not cached in a module variable between requests
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 against the running server. CRITICAL ORDERING observed: an 8001-char prompt returns 400 INVALID_REQUEST in 4ms — a real Gemini call takes >400ms, so the refusal demonstrably precedes any outbound request; validateChatBody runs before resolveKey, which also means no credential is decrypted for a request that was never going to be sent. Stored key -> 200 keySource='user'. No stored key + env set -> 200 keySource='env' (pre-sprint behaviour preserved). Neither -> 503 NO_KEY, distinct from the generic unconfigured 503. FAILURE CASE: a row whose auth_tag was corrupted via raw SQL fell through to the env key and returned 200 keySource='env' rather than 500, logging only the user id. The decrypted key is returned per request and never cached in a module variable. Also moved this file off Google's documented '?key=' query parameter onto the 'x-goog-api-key' header, closing the leak the file's own catch block warns about.

features.description: Typed error codes on /api/ai/* without breaking the existing response shape
steps: Responses carry { error, code } where code is one of NO_KEY | INVALID_KEY | RATE_LIMITED | PROVIDER_ERROR | EMPTY_RESPONSE
The pre-existing { error } key is still present and unchanged, so nothing reading it breaks
429 from aiChatLimiter carries RATE_LIMITED and a retry-after value the client can render
FAILURE CASE: an unmapped provider failure still returns a 502 with PROVIDER_ERROR rather than an undefined code
Provider-supplied text appears in none of the five bodies
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 — all five codes observed live, none inferred. NO_KEY (503, env key cleared and server restarted so dotenv re-read), INVALID_KEY (400, a wrong key injected at the DB layer), RATE_LIMITED (429, AI_RATE_LIMIT_PER_HOUR temporarily set to 2, third request refused, RateLimit-Reset=3600s present), PROVIDER_ERROR, EMPTY_RESPONSE, plus INVALID_REQUEST for local cap violations. The legacy `error` string is present on every body including the limiter's 429, so nothing reading it breaks. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED during verification: Gemini answers 400 for a rejected key, NOT 401/403, and a bad key is otherwise indistinguishable from a malformed payload — both are HTTP 400 with error.status 'INVALID_ARGUMENT'. Routing on status alone reported a user's bad key as 'Invalid request to AI service', which is unactionable: the user cannot tell the fix is to re-enter their key. Now keyed on error.details[].reason === 'API_KEY_INVALID', measured from real provider responses. A rejected USER key returns 400 INVALID_KEY (actionable); a rejected ENV key returns 503 PROVIDER_ERROR, because the user can do nothing about the org's misconfiguration and should not be told to delete their own key. The limiter's code lives in middleware/rateLimit.ts since that 429 is produced before the route runs.

features.description: Client data layer sends, trims, and maps errors — verified before any UI exists
steps: services/assistant.ts goes through fetchWithAuth, so the 401 refresh-and-replay is inherited rather than reimplemented
useAssistant trims history to the newest 20 before sending, so the server's 400 is a backstop and not the normal path
role is mapped user->user and assistant->model on the way out, and model->assistant on the way back (Gemini says 'model', not 'assistant')
verifiedAt is parsed from an ISO string into a Date at the client edge, not passed around as a string typed as Date
FAILURE CASE: each of the five server codes produces a distinct discriminated error value, exercised from a scratch harness with no UI mounted
FAILURE CASE: a missing candidates[0].content.parts[0].text does not throw — every level of that path is optional
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 headless — 19 tests in services/assistant.test.ts, no UI mounted; full client suite 115 green; npm run build green. Covers: goes through fetchWithAuth (so the single refresh coordinator in lib/authSession.ts is inherited, not duplicated); assistant->model role mapping on the way out; history trimmed to the newest 20 of 35; all six server codes mapped to distinct discriminated errors; an unrecognised code degraded to UNKNOWN rather than passed through; a thrown fetch reported as NETWORK and never as a server verdict; retryAfter read from RateLimit-Reset; non-JSON error body survived; a 200 with no text surfaced as EMPTY_RESPONSE instead of throwing; verifiedAt parsed from ISO string to Date. TEST-QUALITY DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED: the first draft asserted failures with `await fn().catch(e => expect(...))`, which passes VACUOUSLY when nothing throws — the assertion never runs. Rewritten as `await expect(fn()).rejects.toMatchObject({ detail: { code } })`. Then mutation-checked: role mapping was changed to emit 'assistant' and the trim was removed, and the suite failed exactly those two tests before both were restored. BUILD DEFECT FOUND: `constructor(public readonly detail)` is a TypeScript-only parameter property, banned by this client's erasableSyntaxOnly. `tsc --noEmit` accepted it; `npm run build` rejected it with TS1294. Rewritten as an explicit field.

features.description: AssistantPanel mounts as a right-hand slot without disturbing existing pages
steps: AppLayout's main becomes a flex row; Outlet keeps min-w-0
At >=1280px the panel is an inline column and page content reflows rather than overflowing
Below 1280px it is an overlay drawer with a scrim, reusing the existing mobile-nav motion vocabulary
FAILURE CASE: open the panel on Bug Tracker and Projects (DataTable, GanttTrack) — no horizontal page scroll appears at 1280 or 1440
Toggling the panel does not remount or reset the routed page's state
Collapsed/expanded persists in localStorage across reload and across a route change
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 by DOM measurement in the browser pane (screenshots and synthetic clicks do not work on this machine; driven via javascript_tool). Measured at 1280: panel 380px, main 1014->634, hScroll false. Bug Tracker, Projects, Notes, Daily, Dashboard all overflowBy 0. Fresh load at 1024 mounts the DRAWER variant with ds-elev-3 and a scrim, main full width 758. Esc closes and focus returns to the trigger (document.activeElement === trigger). Open state survived a real page reload. Remount probe: a stamped node inside <main> kept the SAME node identity across close+reopen, so the routed page reflows rather than rebuilds. Tokens resolve to Luxe (#ffffff / #222222 surface, #C5F43A active trigger) and zero shadcn neutral utilities appear in the subtree. DEFECT FOUND AND FIXED during verification: xl:block/xl:hidden mounted BOTH variants, putting two elements with id='assistant-panel' in the document and making aria-controls ambiguous; replaced with a matchMedia decision (hooks/useMediaQuery.ts) so exactly one exists — measured 2 before, 1 after. GAP: the live resize swap could not be verified here — the CDP viewport override fires neither 'resize' nor matchMedia 'change' (probe counted 0 of each while matchMedia itself flipped), so the listener path is unproven in a real browser. Mount decision itself is verified at both widths via fresh loads. Re-check on a real resize before Stage 4.

features.description: KeyDialog saves, masks, and deletes a key from the UI
steps: Dialog opens on DS Modal so Radix owns focus management
The key field is type=password and is cleared from component state immediately after a successful save
After save the masked form and verifiedAt are shown; the plaintext is not recoverable from the UI
Delete is gated behind ConfirmDialog, per the design-system rule for destructive actions
FAILURE CASE: saving a bad key shows INVALID_KEY inline and leaves the dialog open with the field intact
A NO_KEY response anywhere renders KeyMissingNotice with a CTA that opens this dialog, rather than a red error
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 against the live API. Dialog opens on the DS Modal with focus trapped inside (activeElement inside the dialog). Field is type=password with autocomplete=off and a reveal toggle. FAILURE CASE: a well-shaped but bogus key left the dialog OPEN with the typed value INTACT and an inline "The provider rejected that API key" — so a typo is fixable rather than requiring a re-paste. Happy path with the real key: mask AIza…dIl0 shown, "Verified 8/16/2026", ACTIVE badge rendered, field cleared on success, and the plaintext key absent from the entire dialog. Delete is gated: clicking Remove opened a ConfirmDialog naming the consequence ("cannot be recovered") rather than deleting immediately. External link carries rel=noopener noreferrer. NOTE: a stale error string appeared to persist after a successful save — investigated and it is NOT a product defect. DS Field wraps its error in AnimatePresence, and this browser pane runs with visibilityState=hidden, so motion exit animations never complete and the node stays mounted. The panel error row, which has no exit animation, correctly showed nothing, proving the underlying state was already cleared.

features.description: Panel is keyboard-complete and announces correctly
steps: Esc closes the panel and returns focus to the toggle that opened it
The toggle carries aria-expanded and aria-controls pointing at the panel
The message list is role=log aria-live=polite; a new assistant reply is announced once, not twice
Tab order runs header -> list -> composer with no traps outside the modal
FAILURE CASE: with prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, the thinking indicator and the panel transition stop animating
Focus is visible on every interactive element in both themes
features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15. Esc closes the panel and focus returns to the trigger (document.activeElement === trigger). Trigger carries aria-expanded (flips true/false) and aria-controls=assistant-panel; the panel carries aria-label="AI assistant". Message list is role=log aria-live=polite aria-relevant="additions text", so a reply is announced once. Tab order within the panel runs header actions -> composer, with disabled controls (New chat on an empty thread, Send on an empty composer) correctly absent from the sequence. Message actions reveal on group-focus-within as well as hover, so a keyboard user is not tabbing to an invisible control. GAP: prefers-reduced-motion could not be exercised — this browser pane offers no way to emulate the media query. The code path is written (useReducedMotion suppresses the thinking-dot animation entirely rather than slowing it) but is UNPROVEN. Re-check on a real browser with reduced motion enabled before Stage 4.

features.notes: VERIFIED 2026-08-15 by a scripted audit that was itself proven to fail. Five gates over components/assistant + AssistantPanel, with comment lines stripped so a rule named inside the doc comment explaining it is not counted as a violation: no hex colour literals, no shadcn neutral tokens, no inline motion literals, no deep design-system imports, no dangerouslySetInnerHTML — all pass. MUTATION-CHECKED: injected text-[#ff0000] and text-muted-foreground into AssistantComposer and the audit failed exactly those two gates with the offending line, then passed again once restored. Computed styles confirm the Luxe scale in both themes: panel #ffffff/#222222 (light/dark-surface), title #222222/#ffffff, subtitle #6b7280/#9ca3af (light/dark-text-secondary), composer well #f3f4f6/#2d2d2d (light/dark-surface-2), send button #C5F43A in BOTH themes (brand-accent is theme-invariant by design). AssistantPanel is absent from the design-system barrel, as required — it is layout chrome, not a primitive.
